directAnswer: You can check if a website is down by using online tools like Down For Everyone Or Just Me or by pinging the website from your command line.
summary: This guide provides methods to determine if a website is down, including using online tools and command line utilities.

sections.heading: Using Online Tools
sections.body: Websites like Down For Everyone Or Just Me allow you to quickly check if a site is down. Simply enter the URL, and the tool will inform you of the site's status.

sections.heading: Using Command Line
sections.body: You can use the ping command in your command line interface to check connectivity. This method is useful for more technical users.

steps.title: Check with Down For Everyone Or Just Me
steps.detail: Visit the website, enter the URL of the site you want to check, and click 'Submit'. The tool will tell you if the site is down or not.

steps.title: Ping the Website
steps.detail: Open your command line interface. Type 'ping [website URL]' and press Enter. If you receive replies, the website is likely up.

faqs.question: What if the website is down for me but not for others?
faqs.answer: This could be due to local network issues or your ISP blocking access to the site.

faqs.question: Are there other tools to check website status?
faqs.answer: Yes, other tools include Is It Down Right Now and Site24x7, which provide similar functionality.

faqs.question: How can I check if my own website is down?
faqs.answer: You can use the same online tools mentioned or set up monitoring services like UptimeRobot to alert you of downtime.

caveats: Some websites may block ping requests, leading to false negatives when using the command line method.
